title: incremental unit mapping allocates a quadratic LCS matrix
summary: KCS computes revision unit reuse by passing prior and current prepared-unit arrays into `map_units()`, which immediately allocates a full `(old_units + 1) * (new_units + 1)` `usize` LCS matrix. A local contributor who controls successive document revisions in an indexed scope can inflate both dimensions and repeatedly exhaust memory or CPU during the operator's normal indexing workflow.

codeEvidence.label: Prepared page vector can grow to inferred page count
codeEvidence.explanation: `pdf_text_pages()` derives a logical page count from the current revision bytes and pads the page vector to that count. That cardinality later controls how many `PreparedUnit` values the current revision contributes to mapping.

codeEvidence.label: One prepared unit is created per recovered PDF page
codeEvidence.explanation: For PDF inputs, the prepared-unit array length follows `pdf_pages.len()`. A large logical page vector therefore becomes a large unit array before revision mapping runs.

codeEvidence.label: Indexing maps complete prior and current unit arrays
codeEvidence.explanation: When a prior normalized instance exists, `run_index_pipeline()` passes the entire previous and current prepared-unit slices into `map_units()` before any later full-versus-incremental mode decision can avoid the comparison.

codeEvidence.label: Mapping immediately invokes the LCS helper
codeEvidence.explanation: `map_units()` performs no unit-count, cell-count, or work-budget check before calling the exact LCS implementation with attacker-influenced dimensions.

codeEvidence.label: Full dynamic-programming matrix is allocated and filled
codeEvidence.explanation: The sink allocates `(m + 1) * (n + 1)` `usize` cells and then performs `m * n` fingerprint comparisons. This cost is paid even when no fingerprints match.

codeEvidence.label: Existing control bounds bytes, not prepared-unit product
codeEvidence.explanation: The closest general resource gate rejects oversized raw files but does not bound `old_units.len()`, `new_units.len()`, or their product before the LCS allocation.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that revision unit alignment must be bounded by unit count, cell count, or an explicit work budget before any all-pairs algorithm executes. KCS instead derives prepared-unit arrays from document contents, loads a prior array for the same path, and calls `lcs_fingerprint_pairs()` without checking the product of the two lengths.

validation.method: static source trace plus bounded synthetic probe
validation.summary: The source trace confirms that prior and current prepared units reach `map_units()` unchanged, and `map_units()` allocates a full LCS matrix. A bounded offline probe reproduced quadratic cell and comparison growth for 64, 128, 256, and 512 unit pairs and computed larger memory estimates without allocation.
assertions: The matrix cell count is exactly `(old_units.len() + 1) * (new_units.len() + 1)`.
The nested loops perform `old_units.len() * new_units.len()` fingerprint comparisons.
A 10,000 by 10,000 mapping needs 100,020,001 `usize` cells, approximately 763.09 MiB of cell storage on 64-bit targets, excluding row overhead.
limitations: Large 10,000-plus unit cases were computed, not allocated.
The minimum host-specific document size and unit-generation pattern needed for reliable denial of service were not fully measured.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust local contributor supplies one large-unit revision that is indexed, then supplies another large-unit revision at the same path. The operator's next index loads the prior normalized instance, maps both complete unit arrays, and allocates or fills the quadratic matrix.

dataflow.summary: revision bytes -> prepared page/unit vector -> prior/current prepared-unit arrays -> `map_units()` -> `lcs_fingerprint_pairs()` -> full LCS matrix
dataflow.source: successive contributor-controlled document revisions in an indexed scope
dataflow.outcome: KCS process memory exhaustion, allocator abort/OOM kill, or prolonged CPU saturation during local indexing

reachability.summary: The path is reached through an operator-mediated local index or reindex workflow when a prior normalized instance exists for the same path and profile.
reachability.attacker: local contributor controlling document revisions in the indexed scope
reachability.entrypoint: `kcs index` processing of a changed file with a prior normalized instance
preconditions: Two indexed revisions each produce sufficiently many prepared units.
The operator runs index or reindex on the affected scope.
The prior normalized instance remains readable.
reachability.outcome: persistent denial of indexing for the affected KCS process/scope

impact.why: A crafted revision pair can request hundreds of megabytes to many gigabytes of matrix storage and force quadratic CPU work during normal indexing.

likelihood.why: The trigger requires two large prepared revisions plus an operator-mediated local indexing workflow rather than a single remote request.

limitations: No confidentiality, authorization, or cross-scope integrity impact was shown.
This is a safe Rust resource-exhaustion issue, not a demonstrated memory-corruption primitive.

remediation.summary: Guard `map_units()` with checked arithmetic and an explicit maximum cell/work budget, move the caller so mapping is skipped when incremental behavior is disabled, and fall back to a deterministic full/changed mapping when exact LCS would exceed budget.
regressionTests: `map_units()` over the cell-count budget returns the fallback without allocating the LCS matrix.
A CLI pipeline test with `incremental.enabled = false` confirms no unit mapping is computed for a prior instance.
Two high-unit revisions complete through the safe fallback instead of exhausting memory.
